startup.name: Doe
startup.one_liner: The boring stuff, handled. Everything else, supercharged.
startup.description: Doe is a workspace where AI agents do your work: users connect their tools, describe what they need, and agents handle it, while Doe also helps with work done by hand. Tags are generative AI, SaaS, productivity and data visualization. Two founders in San Francisco, Summer 2025 batch. Forecast window runs 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17, about 16.4 months.

yc_acceptance.basis: Start from the roughly 1 percent prior (0.6 to 2 percent band). Two founders add a little, but a general purpose agent workspace is the most crowded idea type in 2025, a copyable idea with no wedge cuts the odds (defensibility 1 shut down 50 percent), and no traction is stated. The company is in the Summer 2025 batch, so the figure is for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the pitch is a horizontal agent workspace with no named user, narrow wedge or measured traction, in a space where OpenAI, Notion, Zapier and dozens of funded startups ship the same promise. Partners prefer a specific painful job and a sharp reason this team wins.

anchors.adjustment_reason: The estimate is 1.19 times the window anchor, inside the 1.25 times cap. The lift reflects that general agent startups drew many seeds in 2025 (Pokee $12M, Coworker.ai $13M), but those had named founders or labs, and the odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of about $1M to $3M, often from angels and a pre seed fund; the YC deal of about $500K alone does not count here.
Core institutional seed, matching the 2022 and later median raise of about $3.5M to $4.1M in round_benchmarks.
Large institutional seed, the range where 42 percent of confirmed 2026 raises above $1M landed in the winners test.
Oversized seed driven by a hot AI narrative or a top tier lead; rare and press heavy.

ladder.why_it_fails: Doe most likely fails to raise above $1M in 16 months because a horizontal agent workspace has no wedge, and funds that backed Pokee and Coworker.ai already hold the category. Two person teams like dialtone, zuni and dart show no priced round after the YC deal while taking agent workspaces to market, and without a clear niche investors pass.

ladder.why_it_fails: Growth rounds require a clear category leader. Zapier is the success case and took a decade of steady growth with almost no outside capital, which is a different path from fast venture scaling. Most workspace entrants end in sale or stall before reaching Series C.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in shutdown or a small acquisition because model vendors and large workspace apps bundle agent features for free, leaving a two person company with no distribution advantage. Mindmesh and Dart show the usual result: small notes, long searches for a wedge, and quiet drift rather than a breakout.

killers.risk: No wedge: a horizontal agent workspace is bundled by model vendors and workspace apps
killers.evidence: OpenAI, Notion, Zapier and others already ship agent features, and Doe sells a general promise to a general user.
killers.mitigation: Pick one job such as finance close or recruiting ops and win it end to end.

killers.risk: Agent reliability and trust: agents that act on connected tools make costly errors
killers.evidence: Users hesitate to grant write access to email and calendars, and a few failures cause churn.
killers.mitigation: Start with read and draft actions and add approvals.

killers.risk: Fast follower funding: rivals with $12M to $13M seeds can outspend
killers.evidence: Pokee and Coworker.ai raised $12M and $13M seeds in 2025, giving them hiring and marketing power.
killers.mitigation: Reach profitability on a niche and use revenue as the signal.

competition_now.name: Pokee AI
competition_now.what: General purpose agent over thousands of tools

technical_complexity.rationale: Wiring agents to many tools with reliable permissions and error handling is medium hard work that two engineers can prototype in months; the difficulty is in dependability at scale and model dependence on vendors.

takeover_risk.rationale: Model vendors and workspace apps already ship agent features and could match any general workflow within months, with far larger distribution.

evidence.claim: Agent startups raised $12M and $13M seeds in 2025 (Pokee, Coworker.ai), showing investor demand for the category.
Pokee targets agents acting across thousands of tools, the same promise Doe makes, and was funded by Point72 plus strategic investors.

roadmap.goal: Show a user group that depends on it weekly

roadmap.proof: $20K monthly revenue and a lead investor

actions: Add integrations that raise switching costs
roadmap.proof: $1M ARR and net revenue retention above 100 percent

pros.evidence: Seeds of $12M and $13M in 2025 show appetite.

pros.point: Two founders in San Francisco can iterate quickly with low costs
pros.evidence: Agent products rely on vendor models so capital needs are small at the start.

brand.rationale: A three letter name that echoes doing work is easy to say, like short YC names such as Rippling style brands need a story, but it is hard to search and carries the placeholder John Doe feeling, so brand is neutral.

narrative.headline: A general agent workspace from two founders in a crowded and well funded category, with a middling chance of a seed above $1M in 16 months.
narrative.general_summary: Doe promises agents that do your work across connected tools. Investor appetite in 2025 is real, with seeds of $12M and $13M, but those rounds went to teams with named backgrounds, and the product here is horizontal with no wedge, vendor bundling risk and no stated traction. The 16.4 month window is long enough for a typical seed to land, so the number sits near the window adjusted cohort anchor with a small lift. The odds do not rank this company against others in the batch.

assumptions: Only the input file and market searches were used; no revenue or investor data is known.
Seed means an outside round above about $1M closing between 2025-07-07 and 2026-11-17.
Series A given seed is for the same window; Series B and C are ever figures.
Coverage: 662 researched companies; funding data partial.
